nodes.summary: Two elements $p$ and $q$ of a partial order $\mathbb{P}$ are compatible if there is $r \in \mathbb{P}$ with $r \le p$ and $r \le q$.
nodes.title: Compatible conditions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. Write $M_c$ for the set of $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union lies in $M$, and $M_s$ for the set of $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy lies in $M$. nodes.title: (M, ℙ)-generic conditions

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ of elements of a partial order $\mathbb{P}$ is predense below $q \in \mathbb{P}$ if for every $r \le q$ there is $a \in A$ such that $r$ and $a$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Predense below a condition

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and let $X$ be the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$; for $M \subseteq X$ write $M_c$ for the set of $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in $X$ lies in $M$. Then $\mathbb{P}$ is proper if there is a club $C$ in $[X]^\omega$ such that for every $M \in C$ and every $p \in M_c$ there is an $(M, \mathbb{P})$-generic condition $q \le p$. nodes.title: Proper partial orders

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The conditions in $M$ form the set $M_c$ of those $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$; informally, $M_c = M \cap \mathbb{P}$.
nodes.title: Conditions in a model

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The sets of conditions in $M$ form the family $M_s$ of those $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$; informally, $M_s = M \cap \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$.
nodes.title: Sets of conditions in a model

nodes.summary: For every proper partial order $\mathbb{P}$, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\aleph_1$ dense subsets of $\mathbb{P}$, and every condition $p \in \mathbb{P}$, there is a filter $G \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ with $p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$, that is, $G \cap D \neq \emptyset$ for every $D \in \mathcal{D}$.
nodes.title: Proper Forcing Axiom

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
